assortment: Two mixed-form spatial-storage artifacts per quality. Form does not determine quality; construction, material and spatial assembly do.

reference_images.role: Style reference only: painted item silhouettes, dark outlines, compact shading and material highlights. Do not include sheet labels or copy the pictured items.
Palette compatibility reference only. The six large frames numbered quality-1 through quality-6 are already separate UI assets. Do not paint frames into the icon.

common_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one Chinese cultivation RPG inventory icon for Mo Fa Xun Xian.
Primary request: create exactly one Naxu spatial-storage artifact in the form specified by Subject. Storage artifacts may be pouches, boxes, pendants, gourds, vessels, rings, seals, mirrors, orbs or miniature cauldrons; do not automatically convert them into a pouch or ring. The world is a resource-scarce declining cultivation era with recovered ancient artifacts. Names and designs are art proposals only, without new lore, capacities or gameplay rules.
Style/medium: polished hand-painted 2D mobile-game item art matching the provided style reference: bold clean dark outlines, broad readable light and shadow, tactile material highlights, slightly stylized proportions and small signs of age. Maintain the same rendering finish at every tier; ordinary items are well drawn but simply made. Painted art, not pixel art, vector clip art or photorealistic 3D.
Scene/backdrop: genuinely transparent background with real alpha. No scenery, floor, pedestal, ground shadow, colored square, checkerboard or white backdrop.
Composition/framing: one complete centered artifact, near-front three-quarter view, soft upper-left illumination. Final PNG 112 by 112 pixels, occupying two by two 56-pixel inventory cells. Total silhouette including suspended components and effects must fit within 88 to 96 final pixels, with at least 8 transparent pixels on every side. Keep equivalent apparent scale across tiers. Identify quality through construction, not a larger object or larger aura. Keep the object's defining opening, neck, handle or lid readable. Ring finger holes remain clearly open. Attached or suspended parts described in Subject belong to this single assembled artifact, not separate loot.
Rarity design grammar: Q1 normal white = plain soft or simple solid construction, matte common material, no jewel or magic. Q2 excellent green = shaped natural jade or careful handcraft, one broad fitting, no metal armor or glow. Q3 fine blue = clearly rigid metal reinforcement, angular shoulders, one large inset, light only inside that inset. Q4 rare purple = raised stepped architecture, prominent sculpted mount and a visible luminous assembly seam, all parts physically connected. Q5 epic gold = refined metallic gold construction with two visibly separated suspended assembly parts and a crisp gold spatial mechanism. Q6 legendary red = crimson and near-black structure, a clearly visible dark spatial core and three separated suspended seal parts; antique gold is secondary. The tier-specific silhouette and assembly must still differ in grayscale and without a quality frame. Do not solve rarity with recoloring, more scratches, tiny embroidery or simply brighter glow. Never give lower tiers the structures reserved for higher tiers. Epic reads as metallic gold, not orange; legendary reads as red and black, not a second gold tier.
Thumbnail readability: prioritize two to four major masses, bold fittings and clean negative gaps. Major distinguishing features should span at least 8 final pixels; important assembly gaps about 3 final pixels. No dense filigree, hairline seals or particle clouds. Magic, where requested, is a sharply bounded line or solid rim on the artifact, never soft haze that conceals it. High tiers need visibly different physical construction even with effects removed.
Text: none.
Constraints: no letters, numerals, labels, capacity or durability markings, readable runes, rarity badges, UI frame, border, inventory grid, watermark, logo, characters, hands, unrelated props, weapons, coins, loose loot or multi-icon collage. No flames, explosions, sprawling portals or ornamental spikes. Do not copy or merely recolor the reference items. Do not bake a quality frame into the image. Preserve true transparency when saving.

assets.subject: Q1 normal white: Su Ma Naxu Pouch. Silhouette: a squat, soft pear-shaped linen sack with sloping shoulders, one narrow gathered neck and a single thick cord knot. Material: warm off-white coarse hemp cloth, gray-brown cord, two broad folds and one plainly sewn repair patch. The patch is a broad readable shape, not embroidery. The empty front surface and yielding uneven cloth volume are the defining low-tier features. Render it carefully but make the construction unmistakably humble and practical. Hard limits: no jade, gemstone, metal plates, decorative borders, spatial seal display, suspended components or glow. Do not upgrade the simple bag into a jeweled treasure pouch.

Q1 normal white: Hui Mu Naxu Box. Silhouette: a squat rectangular wooden palm box with a plain flat lid, blunt corners and one broad gray cord wrapped around the middle. Ash-gray weathered wood, a few large grain marks and one dull iron latch. Keep the lid line and box depth obvious, with no ornate feet or shaped corner fittings. This is a modest working storage artifact, not a pirate chest or a jeweled reliquary. Hard limits: no jade, gemstone, metal casing, carved relief, spatial aperture, suspended components or glow. The simple unarmored rectangle must remain obvious without color.

Q2 excellent green: Qing Yu Naxu Pendant. Silhouette: one broad rounded-square celadon jade pendant, with a large circular opening near the top and one short knotted cord. Its single solid slab and smoothly rounded rim are clearly visible. One broad shallow cloud-shaped groove crosses the lower face; the rest is uninterrupted polished jade with pale green material highlights and a darker green center. Carefully carved natural material makes this visibly more refined than plain wood or hemp, but still straightforward handcraft. Hard limits: no metal casing, mounted jewel, stacked layers, deep spatial core, suspended components or magical glow. Keep the top opening clear; no tiny tassels.

Q2 excellent green: Qing Teng Naxu Gourd. Silhouette: a stout natural double-lobed gourd with a small upper bulb, broad lower bulb, pinched waist and a clearly seated wooden stopper. Muted green lacquer over a natural shell, one thick woven vine belt at the waist and a single pale jade fastening bead. The natural curved outline, visible stopper and tidy handcrafted binding are the main features. A few broad curved highlights suggest a carefully finished but ordinary material. Hard limits: no metal armor, mounted spatial medallion, layered lid mechanism, floating parts or glow. No liquid, pouring stream or potion effects. Keep ties short.

Q3 fine blue: Xuan Wen Naxu Casket. Silhouette: a compact blue hexagonal casket with broad chamfered corners, a thick fitted silver lid and four visibly raised metal corner guards. The angular reinforced outline must contrast strongly with the plain Q1 wooden box. Deep cobalt lacquer panels sit inside a continuous steel-silver structural skeleton; one large diamond-shaped blue-jade lock occupies the front. A single cyan geometric groove glows only inside that lock. The reinforced corners and prominent lock must survive thumbnail reduction. Hard limits: no gold, raised multi-tier altar, suspended lid, orbiting components or external aura. All parts are physically fitted together.

Q3 fine blue: Liu Wen Naxu Flask. Silhouette: a sealed squat octagonal blue-jade vessel with a short narrow neck, fitted silver cap, broad angular shoulders and two thick silver ribs descending to a silver foot. One large circular blue inset is set into its front as a storage seal, with a small cyan line confined inside the inset. Opaque jade and substantial cold-metal fittings make the body look engineered rather than organically grown. Keep the cap, shoulders and eight-sided belly distinct. Hard limits: no gold, stacked ceremonial mount, floating cap, levitating parts or external light. No visible liquid, potion contents, label or pouring action.

Q4 rare purple: Zi Que Naxu Seal. Silhouette: a substantial square violet-jade seal artifact with a clearly stepped two-tier plinth and a thick sculpted arch handle rising from its top. Blackened silver clasps embrace the four broad corners, while a raised circular violet crystal sits prominently on the front. One crisp violet luminous seam runs between the two connected base tiers, visually separating their stepped profiles. The arch opening and terrace-like base are the defining quality features, substantially more elaborate than a simple reinforced vessel. Hard limits: every part remains physically joined; no gold casing, hovering layers, detached plates or dark void core. No writing or stamped characters.

Q4 rare purple: Zi Que Naxu Ring. Silhouette: a broad blackened-silver finger band carrying a tall stepped two-tier violet crystal mount, with two generous sculpted arch shoulders supporting it. The raised square lower tier and beveled purple upper crystal create an unmistakable architectural top profile, rather than a low ordinary jewel setting. A single crisp violet seam lights the joint between the connected mount layers. Keep the large open finger hole clearly visible beneath the mount; it must remain a wearable ring rather than a crown or a separate altar. Hard limits: all tiers physically connected, no suspended parts, gold body, dark void core, spikes or particle cloud.

Q5 epic gold: Jin Que Naxu Gourd. Silhouette: a stout double-lobed gourd enclosed in a precisely fitted, openwork metallic-gold exoskeleton with two broad curved shoulder fins integrated into the shell. Dark-gold recesses separate champagne-gold polished plates. Its lid and one thick waist collar are the two suspended assembly parts: the lid floats directly above the neck, and the collar floats around the waist, each separated by a clear approximately 3-final-pixel gap. A bold nested gold geometric seal is recessed in the front. This must be structurally transformed from the Q2 natural vine-bound gourd, not merely painted gold. Gold construction dominates; no orange flame. Keep the double-lobed body recognizable. No dark void core or third suspended part; no background halo.

Q5 epic gold: Jin Que Naxu Mirror. Silhouette: a thick octagonal hand-sized gold mirror artifact, without a long handle, with four broad stepped corners and a clearly inset amber-gold face. Two solid crescent-shaped gold locking plates are suspended immediately beside opposite edges; clean dark gaps distinguish the plates from the central body. These are mechanical parts of this one artifact, not decorative rays. The face contains a large readable nested-diamond spatial diagram made of just two bold geometric contours. Broad champagne-gold highlights, deep bronze recesses and a contained pale-gold seal line. Metal construction and separated assembly establish the epic tier. No landscape reflection, face reflection, dark void core, red palette, background magic circle or mist.

Q6 legendary red: Chi Xiao Naxu Orb. Silhouette: a compact spherical crimson-jade storage artifact whose three broad curved outer shell plates are suspended apart around one clearly visible near-black spatial core. The three plates form a broken spherical enclosure, with generous readable gaps, rather than a continuous ordinary bead. A nested square-within-diamond red seal sits at the dark core; the core occupies about one quarter of the object's width and is visibly deep, not a painted black speck. Crimson outer plates, black inner facets and a few antique-gold clamps; gold stays below one fifth of the visible material. A sharp vermilion inner rim follows the core and three short seal links bridge the plate gaps. The impossible spatial assembly must read even without light. No starfield, eyeball, flame, explosion, particle cloud or large portal; every component stays close to this one orb.

Q6 legendary red: Chi Xiao Naxu Cauldron. Silhouette: a palm-sized squat square-bellied crimson storage ding with two thick arch handles, three short near-black feet and a bold stepped roof-like lid. Three suspended assembly parts belong to it: the lid directly above the mouth, plus two broad angular seal plates close to the shoulders, all with clean visible gaps. The front has a large near-black recessed spatial aperture surrounded by nested red geometric seal terraces; the dark core is clearly visible and about one quarter of the body width. Crimson enamel and red jade dominate over near-black structural metal, with antique gold restricted to a few clamps. The body remains an obvious miniature ding despite its impossible spatial lock. Use a crisp vermilion line around the recessed core and seal joints. No cooking contents, smoke, flames, giant temple, separate base, particle storm or background portal.
